title: Opportunity-adjusted RICE + CLAM: a combined prioritization model for latency-aware roadmap tradeoffs
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: PMs and Eng teams at Redwood repeatedly face tradeoffs between maximizing user-facing impact and minimizing long-term inference cost and latency. Existing RICE scoring is useful but treats effort and confidence in isolation from runtime economics. This ticket documents and proposes an "opportunity-adjusted RICE + CLAM" model (RICE-O + CLAM) to combine traditional RICE with a cost/latency alignment metric so we consistently prioritize initiatives that improve product outcomes and inference unit economics together.

Goal: Provide a repeatable, audited scoring process for roadmap planning and cycle prioritization that: 1) surfaces high-impact, low-cost initiatives (optimization wins), 2) penalizes high-cost/low-latency-benefit projects, 3) ties directly to OKRs (latency, cost per token, reliability), and 4) is implementable in our roadmap spreadsheet and Console prioritization view.

What this doc contains:
- A step-by-step scoring guide (how to score Reach/Impact/Confidence/Effort).
- A new CLAM (Cost-Latency Alignment Metric) with scoring bands and weighting guidance.
- The combined formula: RICE-O = (Reach * Impact * Confidence / Effort) * OpportunityMultiplier * CLAM_weighted_factor.
- Examples with two sample initiatives and expected rank changes vs vanilla RICE.
- Operational instructions: artifacts to attach, required reviewers, and rollout to PM team and GTM.

Definition of parts: 
- Reach: number of monthly active routes/customers affected in next 6 months. Use Console telemetry or sales-eng list. (score 1-100)
- Impact: expected delta on OKR metric (0.1 low to 3 high). For qualitative features map to expected % delta.
- Confidence: evidence quality (data, experiment, customer requests) 0.2 to 1.0.
- Effort: engineering points (1-40). Use normalized points; lower = better.
- OpportunityMultiplier: captures business timing/opportunity window (0.5 - 2.0). High if winning early matters (e.g., partner launch).

Introducing CLAM (Cost-Latency Alignment Metric):
- Purpose: quantify whether a given initiative improves unit economics or latency in proportion to its impact. CLAM is deliberately coarse to be applied quickly.
- Inputs (each 0-10):
  1) Cost improvement potential (C): 0=no change, 10=large (>40%) expected per-token savings.
  2) Latency sensitivity alignment (L): how much the feature's user value degrades with added latency (0=not sensitive, 10=very sensitive).
  3) Regression risk multiplier (R): risk of introducing negative regressions (0 low risk, 10 high risk).

- CLAM raw score = (C * 0.5 + L * 0.4 - R * 0.1) => normalized to 0.0-10.0 band.
- CLAM factor = 1 + ((CLAM_raw - 5) / 10) so: CLAM_raw=5 -> factor=1.0 ; CLAM_raw=8 -> factor=1.3 ; CLAM_raw=2 -> factor=0.7.

Combined formula (RICE-O):
- BaseRICE = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort
- RICE-O = BaseRICE * OpportunityMultiplier * CLAM_factor

Weighting guidance:
- For latency-first OKRs use CLAM_weight_bias = 1.2 (increase CLAM influence by 20%).
- For cost-first OKRs use OpportunityMultiplier bias toward initiatives that unlock unit cost reductions.

Scoring process and attachments (required):
- Attach a short PRD (Confluence link), one-sentence hypothesis, and data sources for Reach/Impact.
- Attach Console dashboard or QuickSight query showing route volumes.
- Attach cost model spreadsheet (Drive link) with baseline per-token cost and projected delta.
- Link to any prior experiments or relevant GitHub PRs.

Acceptance criteria for using this model in planning:
- All PM proposals for Cycle planning must include a completed RICE-O table and CLAM inputs.
- Engineering leads must validate Effort estimates and Risk (R).
- At least one reviewer from Applied ML or Runtime must sign off when CLAM C > 6 or R > 6.

Rollout plan:
1) Pilot in Cycle 48 planning with top 30 candidate initiatives (owners assigned).
2) Collect feedback from Eng, Runtime, Applied ML; refine CLAM weights after pilot.
3) Add RICE-O columns to the roadmap spreadsheet and Console planning UI (follow-up ticket).

activity: 2025-11-05: Initial alpha model shared with PM guild — received requests to clarify how to score Confidence and R. Action: added guidance and examples.
2025-12-10: Engineering review (Diego Alvarez & Ravi Patel) — asked for stricter acceptance criteria when CLAM indicates high regression risk. Added mandatory runtime sign-off when R > 6.
2026-01-09: Applied ML feedback — recommended widening Cost improvement buckets for quantization and batching proposals. Updated C weight to 0.5 in CLAM formula.
2026-02-18: Finance provided per-token cost thresholds and asked to include revenue uplift sensitivity. Added OpportunityMultiplier guidance to capture partner timing.
2026-03-03: Pilot scoring run completed for 30 initiatives; summary deck uploaded to Confluence (link in PRD). Early signal: several infra optimizations moved up 4 ranks vs vanilla RICE.
2026-03-10: Submitted for PM guild review and Console product team to discuss adding RICE-O columns to planning UI.
